terminal_name: Puerto de la Luz LNG Terminal
issue: GEM has this Totisa Holdings project as 'proposed' (LastUpdated 2025-06-18), but it now appears effectively dead. The Canary Islands Government's Directorate General for Ecological Transition issued an UNFAVOURABLE environmental impact declaration (DIA desfavorable) on 2025-10-15, after which Totisa Energia S.L.U. withdrew (desistio de) its port-concession application; the Las Palmas Port Authority board accepted the withdrawal and returned the provisional guarantee. Spanish press describe it as 'carpetazo a Totisa' (project shelved/closed). The project had already been formally rejected by the Las Palmas city hall and the Cabildo (island council) in Nov 2024. Direction of travel: proposed -> cancelled (sponsor abandonment after negative environmental ruling).
suggested_action: Reviewer to update lifecycle to cancelled (CancelledYear 2025) via a status_timeline entry — proposed -> cancelled, driven by the 2025-10-15 unfavourable DIA + Totisa concession withdrawal. (Not staged as a Status field edit per sweep rules; fetch_timeline is down.) Sources: infopuertos.com 'Puertos de Las Palmas da carpetazo a Totisa' (PASS, https://infopuertos.com/puertos-de-las-palmas-carpetazo-a-totisa/); infopuertos.com public-consultation background (PASS).

issue: Three different capacity figures circulate and they don't reconcile: (1) GEM = 8.0 bcm/y (= CapacityinMtpa 5.88), sourced to the Enagas physical send-out rate of 800,000 Nm3/h ('up to 8 bcm/y' in Enagas press release + brochure); (2) GIIGNL 2026 lists El Musel at 5.1 mtpa (~6.94 bcm/y) — GIIGNL's own methodology; (3) BOE-A-2024-15568 (Spanish official gazette, 2024-07-26) sets the plant's MAXIMUM ANNUAL regasification capacity at 11,744 GWh/year (raised from 10,969 GWh/y) — a regulatory annual-throughput/allocation cap, a different concept from physical nameplate. GEM's 8 bcm/y is the well-sourced physical nameplate and should NOT be changed off a single reconciliation figure or off the regulatory GWh cap. Flagged for awareness only.
suggested_action: No capacity edit. Optionally footnote in the wiki that the regulatory annual cap is 11,744 GWh/y per BOE-A-2024-15568 (2024-07-26) while the physical send-out is 800,000 Nm3/h (~8 bcm/y). BOE URL verified PASS.
